Mamta Tribedi W/o Shri Mahendra Trivedi filed the FIR at Police Station, Banganga, Indore, District Indore (MP) wherein it was alleged that the present petitioner happens to be of her acquaintance and at his instance, initially on 20.02.2019, she had given a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- (rupees three lakhs) in cash to Vikas Chouksey S/o Shri Vijay Chouksey through the present petitioner towards purchase of a plot (size 25 sq. ft x 50 sq. ft. = 1250 sq. ft.) in Diamond Sector of Kalindi Gold City, Village Bhangya, Tehsil Senwer,

opennyai_summary.19_January_2023__facts:
ORDER This petition under Section 482 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (herein after referred to as "the Code") has been filed by the petitioner seeking quashment of the First Information Report (FIR)
registered vide Crime No.862/2020 dated 23.08.2020 at Police Station Banganga, Indore District Indore (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and the subsequent charge sheet filed against him for the alleged offences as also the other proceedings arising therefrom.
2.
Thereafter, the complainant paid an amount of Rs.1,20,000/- (rupees one lakh twenty thousand) in the account of Ashok Borasi S/o Kailash Chandra Borasi through RTGS; an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- (rupees two lakhs) in cash to Sachin and Vijay Chouksey; and an amount of Rs.65,000/- (rupees sixty five thousand) to Mohit Chouksey through cheque.
However, she came to know that the plot is not in existence and has been defrauded by the aforesaid accused persons.
opennyai_summary.19_January_2023__arguments:
3. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has submitted that even on a bare perusal of the FIR as also the documents filed along with the charge sheet, it is apparent that no case of fraud is made out against the petitioner, as in the FIR, it is specifically stated by the complainant that a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- (rupees three lakhs) was paid to Vikas Chouksey through the petitioner, who had also given her a receipt of the same; and on 20.06.2019 she paid an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- (rupees two lakhs) in cash to Vikas Chouksey.
7. Learned counsel for the objector has also relied upon a decision rendered by the Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal reported as AIR 1992 SC 604 = 1992 Sup. (1) SCC 335.
8.
opennyai_summary.19_January_2023__ANALYSIS:
12. So far as the order dated 28.09.2020 passed by this Court in Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.35552/2020 (Ashok S/o Ramesh Chandra Sharma v. The State of Madhya Pradesh) is Ashok vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152280241/
3
On the aforementioned discussion, this Court has no hesitation to come to a conclusion that further continuance of the proceedings against the present petitioner would be an abuse of process of the Court, as prima facie, no case of 'fraud' for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468,
471 and 120-B of IPC, as alleged in the charge sheet is made out against the present petitioner.
14.
opennyai_summary.19_January_2023__decision:
, this Court finds that a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- (rupees three lakhs) was directed to be deposited by the present petitioner in the trial Court only to ensure the interest of the complainant and it cannot be said that merely because the amount was deposited by the petitioner in his bail application on a direction issued by this Court, it could also be taken as a circumstance against him or her in respect of the offences allegedly committed by the accused persons.
13.
In view of the same, the petition stands allowed; and the FIR registered against the present petitioner vide Crime No.862/2020 dated 23.08.2020 at Police Station Banganga, Indore District Indore (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC and the subsequent charge sheet
as also the further proceedings arising therefrom are hereby quashed, so far as they relate to the present petitioner, and the petitioner stands discharged of the aforesaid alleged offences.
The amount so deposited by the petitioner (while furnishing the bail bonds in Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.35552/2020) be returned back to him; and his bail bonds shall stand discharged.
15. Accordingly, Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.8478/2021 stands allowed and disposed of.
All the other pending interlocutory applications, if any, shall stand disposed of.

opennyai_summary.12_June_2024__facts: This is first application for grant of anticipatory bail under section 438 of Cr.P.C. on behalf of the applicants who are apprehending his arrest in connection with FIR No.476/2018 registered at Police Station Devri, District Sagar for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 419, 467, 468 of IPC.
opennyai_summary.12_June_2024__arguments:
The applicants are a 2 MCRC-24200-2024 permanent resident of district and there is no likelihood of their absconding or tampering with prosecution evidence.
Therefore, prayer has been made to enlarge the applicants on anticipatory bail.
opennyai_summary.12_June_2024__ANALYSIS:
This anticipatory bail application has been argued on the ground that parties had a dispute over the property regarding which a case was filed and compromise was reached between them regarding which statement of both the sides have been recorded.
That accused was a signatory to a will which according to prosecution was forged by the present applicant Ashok.
opennyai_summary.12_June_2024__decision:
It is directed that in the event of arrest of applicants by the police in the aforesaid crime, he shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only)each with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer) for his regular appearance before the Police/Arresting Officer during the investigation or before the Court during trial.
It is directed that the applicants shall abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 438(2) of Cr.P.C., failing which this order shall automatically 3 MCRC-24200-2024 stand cancelled without further reference to the Court.
Accordingly, the M.Cr.C stands allowed and disposed of.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
2. This application for quashing of FIR has been made on the ground that the applicant was not the Director of the Company when the offence was committed and there is no allegations against the applicant in the complaint lodged by the complainant.
The complainant entered into an agreement to purchase Plot No. P-18, admeasuring 40 x 80 sq.ft. at the rate of Rs.1300/- per sq.ft. and an agreement was also executed which was taken back by the Co- accused Sunil Mandwani by taking the complainant into confidence that the same is required for showing to the Town and Country Planning Office.

1
The trial Magistrate by order dated 18.06.2015 allowed the application filed under Section 156(3)
of Cr.P.C.
5.
opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
To buttress his contention, the counsel for applicant has also relied upon the judgments passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Municipal Corporation of Delhi Vs.
Ram Kishan Rohtagi and Others, reported in (1983) 1 SCC 1 and in the case of State of Haryana and Others Vs. Bhajan Lal and Others, reported in 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335.
6.
It is submitted that after selling the plots in question to various persons and after taking money not only the applicant was also inducted as Director but thereafter the said plots were sold to other persons thereby defrauding the persons who had previously purchased the plots by making payment of money to the applicant as well as Co-Directors.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
It is true that there is no stay in the matter but on account of stay in the connected matter, the investigation could not start.
It is true that certain amount was paid to the Director Sunil Mandwani and at that time the applicant was not the Director but later on the plots for whom the money was already taken by Sunil Mandwani were alienated to other persons after induction of the applicant as a Director.
Since, the plots which were already sold by the Company were sold to other persons without returning the money to the earlier purchaser, therefore, said act would certainly amount to an Ashok vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17324369/
2 offence.
Accordingly, it cannot be said that no offence was committed after the applicant was inducted in the Company as a Director.
